# su - Speech Utils

A comprehensive toolkit for speech recognition, text-to-speech generation, and audio processing with simple, intuitive interfaces.

## Installation

`su` has a **lightweight core** (audio format conversion, flexible audio I/O, and
cover-art embedding) that works out of the box:

```bash
pip install su
```

Heavier / more fragile capabilities are optional extras:

```bash
pip install "su[speech]"   # speech recognition + text-to-speech
pip install "su[ml]"       # librosa feature extraction (MFCC, spectral, tempo)
pip install "su[transcribe]"  # word-timed transcription, also under music (Demucs, faster-whisper, torchaudio)
pip install "su[full]"     # everything
```

Extra imports are **lazy**, so `import su` never fails when an extra is missing —
you only get a precise “install `su[...]`” error if you call a feature that needs
one.

> **System dependency:** decoding/encoding non-WAV formats (mp3, flac, m4a, …)
> uses [**ffmpeg**](https://ffmpeg.org/). Install it with `brew install ffmpeg`
> (macOS), `sudo apt-get install ffmpeg` (Debian/Ubuntu), or from ffmpeg.org.
> WAV and raw-waveform conversions need no ffmpeg.

## Quick Start

### Speech Recognition

```python
import su

# Quick recognition from microphone
text = su.recognize()
print(f"You said: {text}")

# Custom timeout and engine
text = su.recognize(timeout=10, engine="sphinx")

# Transcribe from various audio sources
text = su.transcribe("recording.wav")  # File path
print(f"Audio contains: {text}")

# Transcribe from bytes
with open("audio.wav", "rb") as f:
    audio_bytes = f.read()
text = su.transcribe(audio_bytes)

# Transcribe from file-like object
from io import BytesIO

audio_stream = BytesIO(audio_bytes)
text = su.transcribe(audio_stream)

# Transcribe from live microphone using transcribe
text = su.transcribe({"type": "microphone", "timeout": 5})

# Use offline engine for transcription
text = su.transcribe("recording.wav", engine="sphinx")

# Advanced usage
recognizer = su.SpeechRecognizer(engine="google")
text = recognizer.listen_and_recognize(timeout=10)
```

### Word-timed transcription, also of speech under music

`transcribe_words` gives every word its start and end time, precise enough to anchor annotations, even when the speaker talks over their own instrument (the voice about as loud as the music):

```python
from su import transcribe_words

t = transcribe_words("session.m4a")
for w in t.words:
    print(f"{w.start:6.2f} {w.end:6.2f}  {w.text}")
t.untranscribed  # speech regions no word covers
t.dropped  # segments dropped as Whisper hallucinations ("Subtitles by Amara", "さささ")
```

Four steps, each a keyword argument with a working default: `decode` (ffmpeg), `separate` (Demucs `htdemucs` vocals), `recognise` (faster-whisper `large-v3`, Silero VAD at 0.3, no initial prompt, no conditioning on previous text) and `align` (torchaudio `MMS_FA` forced alignment, a spoken letter aligned by its name, “B” as “bee”). For plain speech pass `separation=False`; to keep Whisper’s own times pass `alignment=False` (they are kept beside the aligned ones anyway, as `whisper_start`/`whisper_end`). A smaller model: `recognise=whisper_recogniser(model="small")`. Needs the `transcribe` extra; models are downloaded on first use. Known limit: a single spoken letter under a chord is still unreliable across runs.

### Text-to-Speech

```python
import su

# Quick speech
su.speak("Hello, world!")

# Custom voice settings
su.speak("Slow and quiet", rate=100, volume=0.5)

# Read text from file (path starting with /)
su.speak("/path/to/speech.txt")

# Save to file without hearing
su.speak("Save this", egress="output.wav", send_to_speakers=False)

# Get audio bytes for custom use
audio_bytes = su.speak("Test", egress=lambda x: x, send_to_speakers=False)

# Both save and hear
su.speak("Hello", egress="greeting.wav", send_to_speakers=True)

# Advanced usage
tts = su.TextToSpeech(rate=150, volume=0.8)
tts.speak("This is a test", save_to="output.wav")

# List available voices
voices = tts.get_voices()
for voice in voices:
    print(f"Voice: {voice['name']} ({voice['lang']})")
```

### Partial Application for Custom Functions

```python
import su
from functools import partial

# Create custom recognizer functions
fast_recognize = partial(su.recognize, timeout=2, engine="google")
offline_recognize = partial(su.recognize, engine="sphinx")

# Create custom speech functions
robot_voice = partial(su.speak, rate=300, volume=1.0)
quiet_voice = partial(su.speak, rate=150, volume=0.3)

# Create custom transcription functions
offline_transcribe = partial(su.transcribe, engine="sphinx")
google_transcribe = partial(su.transcribe, engine="google")

# Use them
text = fast_recognize()  # Quick 2-second recognition
robot_voice("I am a robot")  # Fast, loud speech
text = offline_transcribe("audio.wav")  # Offline transcription
```

### Audio Processing

```python
import su

# Load and analyze audio
audio, sample_rate = su.AudioProcessor.load_audio("speech.wav")
features = su.AudioProcessor.extract_features(audio, sample_rate)

print(f"MFCC shape: {features['mfcc'].shape}")
print(f"Tempo: {features['tempo']} BPM")

# Convert audio formats
su.AudioProcessor.convert_format("input.mp3", "output.wav")
```

### 🖼️ Embed Cover Art

Give it some audio and an image — as files (of various formats) or as Python
objects — and get back an audio file with the image embedded as cover art.

```python
import su

# File in → cover embedded, format preserved (mp3 stays mp3).
# The original is NOT overwritten by default:
out = su.embed_image("song.mp3", "cover.jpg")
# -> Path("song_with_image.mp3")

# Replace the original in place when you ask for it:
su.embed_image("song.flac", "cover.png", overwrite=True)

# Choose the output format and location explicitly:
su.embed_image("song.wav", "cover.jpg", output="album/track.m4a")

# Python objects work too — a numpy waveform + a PIL image.
# With no source file format, output defaults to FLAC, written to your
# Downloads folder (override with output_dir=...):
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

waveform = np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2, 16000).astype("float32")
su.embed_image(waveform, Image.open("cover.png"))
# -> Path("~/Downloads/audio_with_image.flac")
```

Embeddable formats: **mp3, flac, m4a/mp4, aiff, ogg, opus** (`su.EMBEDDABLE_FORMATS`).
When the input format can’t hold cover art (e.g. wav) or there’s no file format
at all, the output falls back to FLAC unless you pass `output_format`.

### 🔀 Flexible Audio I/O (Casting)

The casting layer follows Postel’s principle — *be liberal in what you accept,
strict in what you emit*. Any audio representation (path, encoded bytes, a
file-like object, a numpy waveform, a `(waveform, sample_rate)` pair, a list of
samples, or a `pydub.AudioSegment`) casts to the type you need; you control the
output format when it matters.

```python
import su
import numpy as np

# A numpy waveform → an AudioSegment (the canonical in-memory hub):
seg = su.to_audio_segment(np.zeros(8000, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)

# Any source → a (waveform, sample_rate) pair for DSP/ML:
waveform, sr = su.to_waveform("song.mp3", sample_rate=16000, mono=True)

# Any source → WAV bytes (no ffmpeg needed for WAV output):
wav_bytes = su.to_wav_bytes(seg)

# Control the output format on the way out — or omit `output` to get bytes to pipe:
su.export_audio(seg, "out.flac")  # writes FLAC, returns the Path
mp3_bytes = su.export_audio(seg, format="mp3", bitrate="192k")  # returns bytes
```

Under the hood this is an [`i2.castgraph`](https://github.com/i2mint/i2)
transformation graph: every input kind routes **to** the `AudioSegment` hub and
every output is derived **from** it, with multi-hop routes composed
automatically.

## Features

### 🎤 Speech Recognition

- **Multiple Engines**: Google, Sphinx, Wit.ai, Azure, Houndify
- **Live Recognition**: Real-time microphone input
- **File Transcription**: Support for various audio formats
- **Noise Handling**: Automatic ambient noise adjustment

### 🔊 Text-to-Speech

- **Cross-Platform**: Works on Windows, macOS, Linux
- **Voice Control**: Rate, volume, and voice selection
- **File Export**: Save speech to audio files
- **Multiple Voices**: Access to system voices

### 🎵 Audio Processing

- **Format Conversion**: MP3, WAV, FLAC, and more
- **Feature Extraction**: MFCC, spectral features, tempo
- **ML Ready**: Features suitable for machine learning
- **Librosa Integration**: Advanced audio analysis

### 🖼️ Cover Art

- **Embed Images**: mp3, flac, m4a/mp4, aiff, ogg, opus
- **Format-Preserving**: keeps the input format when it supports embedding
- **Safe by Default**: never overwrites the original unless you ask
- **Flexible Inputs**: audio and images as files or Python objects

### 🔀 Flexible I/O (Casting)

- **Postel’s Principle**: liberal inputs, strict, annotatable cores
- **Many Representations**: paths, bytes, file-like, numpy waveforms, AudioSegment
- **Controllable Output**: choose the output format, or pipe raw bytes
- **castgraph-Powered**: canonical `AudioSegment` hub with auto-routed conversions

## API Reference

### Convenience Functions

```python
# Speech recognition with customizable settings
text = su.recognize(timeout=5, engine="google")

# Flexible text-to-speech with multiple input/output options
result = su.speak(text_src, rate=200, volume=0.9, egress=None, send_to_speakers=True)

# Where text_src can be:
# - "Hello world" (direct text)
# - "/path/to/file.txt" (file path - must start with / or drive letter)
# - Path("file.txt") (Path object)
# - StringIO("text") (file-like object)
# - text_iterator() (iterator yielding text chunks)

# Where egress can be:
# - None (default - no special output)
# - "output.wav" (save to file path)
# - lambda x: x (return audio bytes)
# - custom_function (process audio bytes)

# Flexible audio transcription with multiple source types
text = su.transcribe(audio_src, engine="google")
```

### SpeechRecognizer

```python
recognizer = su.SpeechRecognizer(engine="google")

# Listen from microphone
text = recognizer.listen_and_recognize(timeout=5)

# Transcribe file
text = recognizer.recognize_file("audio.wav")
```

### TextToSpeech

```python
tts = su.TextToSpeech(rate=200, volume=0.9)

# Speak text
tts.speak("Hello world")

# Save to file
tts.speak("Save this", save_to="output.wav")

# Change voice
voices = tts.get_voices()
tts.set_voice(voices[0]["id"])
```

### AudioProcessor

```python
# Load audio
audio, sr = su.AudioProcessor.load_audio("file.wav")

# Extract ML features
features = su.AudioProcessor.extract_features(audio, sr)

# Convert format
su.AudioProcessor.convert_format("input.mp3", "output.wav")
```

## Dependencies

**Core** (always installed):

- **i2**: the `castgraph` transformation engine behind flexible casting
- **pydub**: audio format conversion (via ffmpeg)
- **numpy**: waveform / numerical operations
- **mutagen**: reading/writing audio metadata (cover art)
- **Pillow**: image handling for cover art

**Extras** (opt in):

- **`su[speech]`** → `SpeechRecognition`, `pyttsx3`, `pyaudio` — recognition + TTS
- **`su[ml]`** → `librosa`, `soundfile` — feature extraction / analysis

## System Requirements

### FFmpeg (for non-WAV audio)

Decoding/encoding mp3, flac, m4a, ogg, etc. uses **ffmpeg**:

- **macOS**: `brew install ffmpeg`
- **Debian/Ubuntu**: `sudo apt-get install ffmpeg`
- **Windows / other**: download from https://ffmpeg.org/

WAV and raw-waveform conversions work without ffmpeg.

### For Speech Recognition (`su[speech]`):

- **Windows / macOS**: no additional system requirements
- **Linux**: `sudo apt-get install flac portaudio19-dev` (FLAC + PortAudio for the microphone)

## Examples

### Voice Assistant with Custom Settings

```python
import su
from functools import partial

# Create optimized functions for the assistant
quick_listen = partial(su.recognize, timeout=3, engine="google")
assistant_voice = partial(su.speak, rate=180, volume=0.8)

while True:
    print("Listening...")
    text = quick_listen()

    if text:
        print(f"You said: {text}")
        response = f"You said: {text}"
        assistant_voice(response)

    if text and "goodbye" in text.lower():
        assistant_voice("Goodbye!")
        break
```

### Audio Analysis Pipeline

```python
import su
import numpy as np

# Load audio file
audio, sr = su.AudioProcessor.load_audio("speech.wav")

# Extract features for ML
features = su.AudioProcessor.extract_features(audio, sr)

# Use MFCC features (common for speech recognition)
mfcc_features = features["mfcc"]
mfcc_mean = np.mean(mfcc_features, axis=1)

print(f"MFCC feature vector shape: {mfcc_mean.shape}")
```

### Batch Processing with Different Engines

```python
import su
from functools import partial
from pathlib import Path

# Create specialized transcription functions
google_transcribe = partial(su.transcribe, engine="google")  # For online processing
sphinx_transcribe = partial(su.transcribe, engine="sphinx")  # For offline processing

input_dir = Path("audio_files")
output_dir = Path("transcriptions")
output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for audio_file in input_dir.glob("*.wav"):
    print(f"Processing {audio_file.name}...")

    # Try Google first (better accuracy), fallback to Sphinx
    text = google_transcribe(audio_file) or sphinx_transcribe(audio_file)

    # Save transcription
    output_file = output_dir / f"{audio_file.stem}.txt"
    with open(output_file, "w") as f:
        f.write(text or "Transcription failed")
```

### Voice Profile System

```python
import su
from functools import partial

# Define different voice profiles
profiles = {
    "assistant": partial(su.speak, rate=180, volume=0.8),
    "narrator": partial(su.speak, rate=150, volume=0.7),
    "robot": partial(su.speak, rate=250, volume=1.0),
    "whisper": partial(su.speak, rate=120, volume=0.3),
}

# Use different voices for different purposes
profiles["assistant"]("How can I help you today?")
profiles["narrator"]("Once upon a time, in a land far away...")
profiles["robot"]("SYSTEM INITIALIZED. READY FOR COMMANDS.")
profiles["whisper"]("This is a secret message.")

# Save different voice outputs
for name, voice_func in profiles.items():
    voice_func(f"This is the {name} voice.", save_to=f"{name}_sample.wav")
```

### Flexible Audio Sources

The `transcribe()` function accepts audio from multiple sources:

```python
import su
from io import BytesIO

# 1. File paths (strings or Path objects)
text = su.transcribe("recording.wav")
text = su.transcribe(Path("audio/speech.mp3"))

# 2. Raw audio bytes
with open("audio.wav", "rb") as f:
    audio_bytes = f.read()
text = su.transcribe(audio_bytes)

# 3. File-like objects (BytesIO, open files, etc.)
audio_stream = BytesIO(audio_bytes)
text = su.transcribe(audio_stream)

# 4. Open file handles
with open("recording.wav", "rb") as f:
    text = su.transcribe(f)


# 5. Audio chunk iterators
def audio_chunks():
    with open("large_audio.wav", "rb") as f:
        while True:
            chunk = f.read(8192)  # 8KB chunks
            if not chunk:
                break
            yield chunk


text = su.transcribe(audio_chunks())

# 6. Live microphone via transcribe
text = su.transcribe({"type": "microphone", "timeout": 10})

# 7. Network streams or any file-like object
import requests

response = requests.get("https://example.com/audio.wav", stream=True)
text = su.transcribe(BytesIO(response.content))
```

### Batch Processing with Different Sources

```python
import su
from functools import partial
from pathlib import Path
from io import BytesIO

# Create specialized transcription functions
google_transcribe = partial(su.transcribe, engine="google")
sphinx_transcribe = partial(su.transcribe, engine="sphinx")

# Process various audio sources
sources = [
    "local_file.wav",  # File path
    BytesIO(audio_bytes),  # Bytes stream
    {"type": "microphone", "timeout": 3},  # Live microphone
    Path("recordings/interview.mp3"),  # Path object
]

for i, source in enumerate(sources):
    print(f"Processing source {i + 1}...")

    # Try Google first, fallback to Sphinx
    text = google_transcribe(source) or sphinx_transcribe(source)

    print(f"Result: {text or 'Transcription failed'}")
```

# _autosummary/su.base.html.md

# su.base

Base speech functionalities for su: speech recognition and text-to-speech.

This module keeps the *strict, explicit* speech-processing cores small and pairs
each with a *flexible* public wrapper that casts its inputs through
[`su.casting`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#module-su.casting) (Postel’s principle: liberal inputs, strict cores).

The speech features here require the optional `speech` extra
(`pip install "su[speech]"` — brings `SpeechRecognition`, `pyttsx3` and
`pyaudio`) and the `extract_features` analysis needs the `ml` extra
(`librosa`). All such imports are **lazy**, so `import su` and the
audio-casting / cover-art tools work even when those extras are absent; a precise
`MissingDependencyError` is raised only when a feature that
needs them is actually invoked.

### Functions

| [`recognize`](_autosummary/su.base.html.md#su.base.recognize)([timeout, engine])                     | Quick speech recognition from the microphone (needs the `speech` extra).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`speak`](_autosummary/su.base.html.md#su.base.speak)(text_src, \*[, rate, volume, egress, ...]) | Quick text-to-speech with flexible input and output options.               |
| [`transcribe`](_autosummary/su.base.html.md#su.base.transcribe)(audio_src, \*[, engine, debug])       | Quick transcription of audio from any supported source.                    |

### Classes

| [`SpeechRecognizer`](_autosummary/su.base.html.md#su.base.SpeechRecognizer)([engine])   | Easy-to-use speech recognition interface (needs the `speech` extra).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TextToSpeech`](_autosummary/su.base.html.md#su.base.TextToSpeech)([rate, volume]) | Easy-to-use text-to-speech interface (needs the `speech` extra).       |
| [`AudioProcessor`](_autosummary/su.base.html.md#su.base.AudioProcessor)()             | Audio file processing utilities.                                       |

### *class* su.base.AudioProcessor

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Audio file processing utilities.

`load_audio` and `convert_format` use the lightweight core (pydub);
`extract_features` needs the `ml` extra (librosa).

#### *static* convert_format(input_path, output_path, format='wav')

Convert an audio file from one format to another.

* **Parameters:**
  * **input_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Input file path (or any supported audio source).
  * **output_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Output file path.
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Target format (wav, mp3, flac, …). Non-WAV needs ffmpeg.
* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)
* **Returns:**
  True if conversion succeeded, else False.

### Example

```pycon
>>> AudioProcessor.convert_format("input.mp3", "output.wav")
True
```

#### *static* extract_features(audio_data, sample_rate)

Extract basic audio features for ML (needs the `ml` extra).

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio_data** (`ndarray`) – Audio time series.
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Sample rate.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]
* **Returns:**
  Dictionary with MFCC, spectral, tempo and beat features.

### Example

```pycon
>>> audio, sr = AudioProcessor.load_audio("speech.wav")
>>> features = AudioProcessor.extract_features(audio, sr)
```

#### *static* load_audio(file_path, sample_rate=None)

Load audio to a `(waveform, sample_rate)` pair.

Accepts any source [`su.casting.to_waveform()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_waveform) accepts. Uses the
lightweight core (no librosa required).

* **Parameters:**
  * **file_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes) | [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO)) – Audio source (path, bytes, file-like, waveform, …).
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Target sample rate (None keeps the native rate).
* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]
* **Returns:**
  Tuple of (audio_data, sample_rate), audio as float32 mono in [-1, 1].

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from su.casting import to_wav_bytes
>>> wav = to_wav_bytes(np.zeros(8000, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)
>>> audio, sr = AudioProcessor.load_audio(wav)
>>> audio.dtype, sr
(dtype('float32'), 8000)
```

### *class* su.base.SpeechRecognizer(engine='google')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The microphone source, created lazily (needs `pyaudio`).

### Example

```pycon
>>> tts = TextToSpeech()
>>> tts.speak("Hello, world!")
```

### su.base.recognize(timeout=5, , engine='google')

Quick speech recognition from the microphone (needs the `speech` extra).

* **Parameters:**
  * **timeout** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Maximum seconds to wait for speech.
  * **engine** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Recognition engine (‘google’, ‘sphinx’, ‘wit’, ‘azure’, ‘houndify’).
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### Example

```pycon
>>> text = recognize()
```

### su.base.speak(text_src, , rate=200, volume=0.9, egress=None, send_to_speakers=True, output_format=None)

Quick text-to-speech with flexible input and output options.

* **Parameters:**
  * **text_src** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO) | [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Any source accepted by [`su.casting.to_text()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_text) (direct text,
    a text-file path/Path, a file-like object, or an iterable of chunks).
  * **rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Speech rate (words per minute).
  * **volume** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Volume level (0.0 to 1.0).
  * **egress** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – 

    Optional output handler:
    - None: no file/bytes output (just speakers, if enabled).
    - str/Path: file path to save audio; the extension (or
      `output_format`) selects the encoding.
    - Callable: receives the synthesized WAV bytes and its return value
      is returned.
  * **send_to_speakers** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to also play the audio through the speakers.
  * **output_format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Explicit output format for a path `egress` (overrides the
    extension). Where format does not matter, use a callable `egress` to
    pipe the raw bytes.
* **Returns:**
  The egress callable’s result, the written [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path), or None.

### Example

```pycon
>>> speak("Hello, world!")
>>> speak("Save this", egress="out.mp3", send_to_speakers=False)
>>> audio = speak("Test", egress=lambda b: b, send_to_speakers=False)
```

### su.base.transcribe(audio_src, , engine='google', debug=False)

Quick transcription of audio from any supported source.

Non-WAV inputs are transcoded to WAV via [`su.casting.to_wav_source()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_wav_source)
(needs ffmpeg) before being handed to the strict recognition core.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio_src** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes) | [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO) | [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)] | [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – Any source accepted by [`su.casting.to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_audio_segment),
    or a `{'type': 'microphone', 'timeout': N}` dict for live capture.
  * **engine** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Recognition engine (‘google’, ‘sphinx’, ‘wit’, ‘azure’, ‘houndify’).
  * **debug** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Print debug information and re-raise unexpected errors if True.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)
* **Returns:**
  Transcribed text, or None if transcription failed.

### Example

```pycon
>>> text = transcribe("recording.wav")
>>> text = transcribe({'type': 'microphone', 'timeout': 5})
```


# _autosummary/su.casting.html.md

# su.casting

Flexible input/output casting for audio (and text).

Postel’s principle applied to audio: \*be liberal in what you accept, strict in
what the base functions require.\* This module provides a small
`i2.castgraph`-based transformation layer that normalises the many
*representations* an audio resource can take — file paths, encoded bytes,
file-like objects, numpy waveforms, plain sample lists, or a
`pydub.AudioSegment` — into the strict types the base functions consume,
and lets callers control the *output* format when it matters (and pipe raw bytes
when it does not).

## Canonical hub

`pydub.AudioSegment` is the canonical in-memory audio type (the “hub”):
it carries sample rate / channels / sample width, constructs from raw PCM or any
ffmpeg-decodable file/bytes, and exports to any format. Every *input* kind
converts **to** the hub; every *output* is derived **from** it. castgraph composes
multi-hop routes automatically (e.g. `audio_path -> AudioSegment -> wav_source`).

## Kinds

Input kinds:  `'audio_path'`, `'audio_bytes'`, `'audio_file_like'`,
`'waveform'`, `'waveform_sr'`, `'sample_list'`, and the hub
`AudioSegment`.

Output kinds: `'wav_source'`, `'wav_bytes'`, `'waveform_sr'` (+ the hub).

## Public API

- [`to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_audio_segment) — universal ingress to the hub.
- [`to_wav_source()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_wav_source) / [`to_wav_bytes()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_wav_bytes) — WAV for `speech_recognition`.
- [`to_waveform()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_waveform) — `(np.ndarray, sample_rate)` for DSP/ML.
- [`export_audio()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.export_audio) — the egress: choose the output format, or get bytes.
- [`to_text()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_text) — flexible text ingress.
- `audio_graph` — the underlying `TransformationGraph`.

#### NOTE
Decoding/encoding non-WAV formats (mp3, flac, m4a, …) uses **ffmpeg** via
pydub. Install it separately (e.g. `brew install ffmpeg` /
`apt-get install ffmpeg`). WAV and raw-sample conversions need no ffmpeg.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from su.casting import to_audio_segment, to_wav_bytes, to_waveform
>>> # A numpy waveform (int16 PCM) becomes an AudioSegment...
>>> samples = (np.sin(np.linspace(0, 6.28, 8000)) * 16000).astype(np.int16)
>>> seg = to_audio_segment(samples, sample_rate=8000)
>>> seg.frame_rate, seg.channels
(8000, 1)
>>> # ...exports to WAV bytes (no ffmpeg needed)...
>>> to_wav_bytes(seg)[:4]
b'RIFF'
>>> # ...and round-trips back to a (waveform, sample_rate) pair.
>>> wf, sr = to_waveform(seg, dtype='int16')
>>> wf.shape, sr
((8000,), 8000)
```

### Functions

| [`to_audio_segment`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_audio_segment)(src, \*[, sample_rate, ...])    | Cast any supported audio representation to a `pydub.AudioSegment`.                                                         |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`to_wav_source`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_wav_source)(src, \*\*kwargs)                   | Cast `src` to a rewound WAV [`io.BytesIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BytesIO) (for speech_recognition). |
| [`to_wav_bytes`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_wav_bytes)(src, \*\*kwargs)                    | Cast `src` to WAV-encoded [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes).                               |
| [`to_waveform`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_waveform)(src, \*[, sample_rate, mono, dtype]) | Cast `src` to a `(samples, sample_rate)` pair for DSP/ML.                                                                  |
| [`export_audio`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.export_audio)(src[, output, format, ...])         | Egress: encode `src` to a chosen format, returning bytes or a path.                                                        |
| [`to_text`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_text)(text_src)                                | Resolve a flexible text source to a plain `str`.                                                                           |

### su.casting.export_audio(src, output=None, , format=None, sample_rate=None, bitrate=None, tags=None, \*\*export_kwargs)

Egress: encode `src` to a chosen format, returning bytes or a path.

This is the controllable-output half of the casting layer. Where the output
format matters, pass `format` (or an `output` path with an extension);
where it does not, omit `output` to get raw bytes you can pipe.

* **Parameters:**
  * **src** – Any supported audio source.
  * **output** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Destination path. If None, encoded bytes are returned instead.
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Target format (`'wav'`, `'mp3'`, `'flac'`, …). Defaults to
    the `output` path’s extension, else `'wav'`.
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional resample target for raw-sample inputs.
  * **bitrate** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional encoder bitrate (e.g. `'192k'` for mp3).
  * **tags** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional metadata tags passed to pydub’s exporter.
  * **\*\*export_kwargs** – Forwarded to `AudioSegment.export()`.
* **Returns:**
  `bytes` if `output` is None, else the [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) written.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> data = export_audio(np.zeros(800, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)
>>> data[:4]  # WAV by default
b'RIFF'
```

### su.casting.to_audio_segment(src, , sample_rate=None, sample_width=None, channels=None)

Cast any supported audio representation to a `pydub.AudioSegment`.

This is the universal ingress (Postel’s “be liberal in what you accept”).

* **Parameters:**
  * **src** – The audio source. See `_SUPPORTED_INPUTS`.
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Sample rate to *assume* for raw-sample inputs (numpy arrays
    / lists). Ignored for encoded inputs, which carry their own rate.
  * **sample_width** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Bytes per sample for raw-sample inputs (inferred if None).
  * **channels** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Channel count for raw-sample inputs (inferred/defaulted to 1).
* **Return type:**
  `AudioSegment`
* **Returns:**
  The audio as an `AudioSegment`.
* **Raises:**
  [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – If `src` is not a supported audio representation.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> seg = to_audio_segment(np.zeros(1000, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=16000)
>>> seg.frame_rate
16000
>>> to_audio_segment(seg) is seg  # AudioSegment passes through unchanged
True
```

### su.casting.to_text(text_src)

Resolve a flexible text source to a plain `str`.

* **Parameters:**
  **text_src** – 

  One of:
  - `str`: direct text, or a file path if it looks like an absolute
    path (starts with the OS path separator or a Windows drive prefix).
  - [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path): path to a UTF-8 text file.
  - file-like: an object with `.read()` (text or binary).
  - iterable of `str`/`bytes` chunks.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Returns:**
  The resolved text.
* **Raises:**
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If a referenced file cannot be read.
  * [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – If `text_src` is an unsupported type.

### Example

```pycon
>>> to_text("hello world")
'hello world'
>>> from io import StringIO
>>> to_text(StringIO("streamed text"))
'streamed text'
>>> to_text(iter(["a", "b", "c"]))
'abc'
```

### su.casting.to_wav_bytes(src, \*\*kwargs)

Cast `src` to WAV-encoded [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes).

Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to [`to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_audio_segment).

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> to_wav_bytes(np.zeros(800, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)[:4]
b'RIFF'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### su.casting.to_wav_source(src, \*\*kwargs)

Cast `src` to a rewound WAV [`io.BytesIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BytesIO) (for speech_recognition).

Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to [`to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_audio_segment).

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> buf = to_wav_source(np.zeros(800, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)
>>> buf.read(4)
b'RIFF'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`BytesIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BytesIO)

### su.casting.to_waveform(src, , sample_rate=None, mono=True, dtype='float32')

Cast `src` to a `(samples, sample_rate)` pair for DSP/ML.

* **Parameters:**
  * **src** – Any supported audio source.
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Desired sample rate of the returned waveform. For encoded
    inputs the audio is resampled to it; for raw-sample inputs it is the
    assumed rate. If None, the source’s native rate is kept.
  * **mono** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Down-mix to a single channel (returns a 1-D array). If False, a
    2-D `(num_samples, num_channels)` array is returned.
  * **dtype** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Output dtype. Float dtypes are normalised to `[-1.0, 1.0]`;
    integer dtypes keep the raw PCM values.
* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]
* **Returns:**
  `(samples, sample_rate)`.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> wf, sr = to_waveform(np.ones(1000, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=16000)
>>> wf.shape, sr, wf.dtype
((1000,), 16000, dtype('float32'))
```


# _autosummary/su.cover_art.html.md

# su.cover_art

Embed cover images into audio files.

The headline tool, [`embed_image()`](_autosummary/su.cover_art.html.md#su.cover_art.embed_image), takes some *audio* and an *image* — each
given as a file (of various formats) or as a Python object — and produces an
audio file with the image embedded as cover art, for the formats that support it
(mp3, flac, m4a/mp4, aiff, ogg/opus).

Behaviour (all parametrizable):

- **Output format** follows the input format when that format supports
  embedding; otherwise (or when there is no file format, e.g. a numpy waveform)
  it falls back to **flac**. An explicit `output_format` (or an `output` path
  with an extension) overrides this.
- **The original file is never overwritten by default.** Set `overwrite=True`
  to replace it in place (only valid when the output format matches the input’s).
- **Output path** is either the explicit `output` you pass, a name derived from
  the input path (`<stem>_with_image.<ext>` next to it), or — when the input is
  a Python object with no path — a file in `output_dir` (default: the system
  Downloads folder).

When the source is already a file in the target format, its encoded bytes are
copied verbatim (no lossy re-encode) before the image is written in.

#### NOTE
Re-encoding a source into a different format uses **ffmpeg** via pydub. The
metadata write itself uses `mutagen` and needs no ffmpeg.

### Example

```pycon
>>> from su.cover_art import EMBEDDABLE_FORMATS
>>> sorted(EMBEDDABLE_FORMATS)
['aiff', 'flac', 'm4a', 'mp3', 'ogg', 'opus']
```

### Module Attributes

| [`EMBEDDABLE_FORMATS`](_autosummary/su.cover_art.html.md#su.cover_art.EMBEDDABLE_FORMATS)   | The set of audio formats [`embed_image()`](_autosummary/su.cover_art.html.md#su.cover_art.embed_image) can embed images into.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`embed_image`](_autosummary/su.cover_art.html.md#su.cover_art.embed_image)(audio, image, \*[, output, ...])   | Create an audio file with an embedded cover image.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|

### su.cover_art.EMBEDDABLE_FORMATS *= frozenset({'aiff', 'flac', 'm4a', 'mp3', 'ogg', 'opus'})*

The set of audio formats [`embed_image()`](_autosummary/su.cover_art.html.md#su.cover_art.embed_image) can embed images into.

### su.cover_art.embed_image(audio, image, , output=None, output_format=None, overwrite=False, output_dir=None, description='Cover')

Create an audio file with an embedded cover image.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – The audio source — a file path, encoded bytes, a file-like object,
    a numpy waveform / `(waveform, sample_rate)` pair, or a
    `pydub.AudioSegment` (anything [`su.casting.to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_audio_segment)
    accepts).
  * **image** – The cover image — a path, raw image bytes, a file-like object, or a
    PIL `Image`.
  * **output** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Explicit output path. If it has no extension, one is added for the
    resolved format. If None, the path is derived (see module docstring).
  * **output_format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Force the output format (e.g. `'mp3'`, `'flac'`,
    `'m4a'`, `'aiff'`, `'ogg'`, `'opus'`). Overrides the
    input-format-follows rule.
  * **overwrite** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, replace the original file in place (only when the
    output format matches the input’s). Defaults to False — the original
    is never touched.
  * **output_dir** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Directory for derived output paths. Defaults to the input
    file’s directory, or the system Downloads folder for object inputs.
  * **description** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The cover-art description/title stored in the tag.
* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)
* **Returns:**
  The [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) of the written audio file.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If the resolved format cannot embed images, or if
      `overwrite` conflicts with the resolved output.

### Example

```pycon
>>> # File in, cover embedded, format preserved (mp3 stays mp3):
>>> embed_image("song.mp3", "cover.jpg")
PosixPath('song_with_image.mp3')
>>> # Object in (no format) -> flac in Downloads:
>>> import numpy as np
>>> embed_image(np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.int16), "cover.png")
PosixPath('/Users/you/Downloads/audio_with_image.flac')
>>> # Replace the original in place:
>>> embed_image("song.flac", img, overwrite=True)
PosixPath('song.flac')
```


# _autosummary/su.html.md

# su

Speech Utils (su): tools for audio I/O, speech recognition, TTS, and cover art.

The package is organised in three layers:

- [`su.casting`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#module-su.casting) — flexible input/output casting for audio (Postel’s
  principle): normalise paths, bytes, file-like objects, numpy waveforms, sample
  lists, or `AudioSegment` into the strict types the base functions need, and
  control the output format when it matters.
- [`su.base`](_autosummary/su.base.html.md#module-su.base) — speech recognition and text-to-speech (needs the `speech`
  extra) plus lightweight audio processing.
- [`su.cover_art`](_autosummary/su.cover_art.html.md#module-su.cover_art) — embed cover images into audio files.

The lightweight core (audio conversion + cover art) works out of the box.
Heavier capabilities live behind extras: `pip install "su[speech]"` (speech
recognition + TTS) and `pip install "su[ml]"` (librosa feature extraction).
Those imports are lazy, so `import su` never fails when an extra is absent.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import su
>>> import numpy as np
>>> seg = su.to_audio_segment(np.zeros(8000, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)
>>> su.to_wav_bytes(seg)[:4]
b'RIFF'
```

### Functions

| [`recognize`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.recognize)([timeout, engine])                     | Quick speech recognition from the microphone (needs the `speech` extra).                                                   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`speak`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.speak)(text_src, \*[, rate, volume, egress, ...]) | Quick text-to-speech with flexible input and output options.                                                               |
| [`transcribe`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.transcribe)(audio_src, \*[, engine, debug])       | Quick transcription of audio from any supported source.                                                                    |
| [`transcribe_words`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.transcribe_words)(audio, \*[, decode, ...])       | Transcribe `audio` into words with times.                                                                                  |
| [`to_audio_segment`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.to_audio_segment)(src, \*[, sample_rate, ...])    | Cast any supported audio representation to a `pydub.AudioSegment`.                                                         |
| [`to_wav_source`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.to_wav_source)(src, \*\*kwargs)                   | Cast `src` to a rewound WAV [`io.BytesIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BytesIO) (for speech_recognition). |
| [`to_wav_bytes`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.to_wav_bytes)(src, \*\*kwargs)                    | Cast `src` to WAV-encoded [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes).                               |
| [`to_waveform`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.to_waveform)(src, \*[, sample_rate, mono, dtype]) | Cast `src` to a `(samples, sample_rate)` pair for DSP/ML.                                                                  |
| [`export_audio`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.export_audio)(src[, output, format, ...])         | Egress: encode `src` to a chosen format, returning bytes or a path.                                                        |

### *class* su.AudioProcessor

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Audio file processing utilities.

`load_audio` and `convert_format` use the lightweight core (pydub);
`extract_features` needs the `ml` extra (librosa).

#### *static* convert_format(input_path, output_path, format='wav')

Convert an audio file from one format to another.

* **Parameters:**
  * **input_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Input file path (or any supported audio source).
  * **output_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Output file path.
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Target format (wav, mp3, flac, …). Non-WAV needs ffmpeg.
* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)
* **Returns:**
  True if conversion succeeded, else False.

### Example

```pycon
>>> AudioProcessor.convert_format("input.mp3", "output.wav")
True
```

#### *static* extract_features(audio_data, sample_rate)

Extract basic audio features for ML (needs the `ml` extra).

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio_data** (`ndarray`) – Audio time series.
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Sample rate.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]
* **Returns:**
  Dictionary with MFCC, spectral, tempo and beat features.

### Example

```pycon
>>> audio, sr = AudioProcessor.load_audio("speech.wav")
>>> features = AudioProcessor.extract_features(audio, sr)
```

#### *static* load_audio(file_path, sample_rate=None)

Load audio to a `(waveform, sample_rate)` pair.

Accepts any source [`su.casting.to_waveform()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_waveform) accepts. Uses the
lightweight core (no librosa required).

* **Parameters:**
  * **file_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes) | [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO)) – Audio source (path, bytes, file-like, waveform, …).
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Target sample rate (None keeps the native rate).
* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]
* **Returns:**
  Tuple of (audio_data, sample_rate), audio as float32 mono in [-1, 1].

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from su.casting import to_wav_bytes
>>> wav = to_wav_bytes(np.zeros(8000, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)
>>> audio, sr = AudioProcessor.load_audio(wav)
>>> audio.dtype, sr
(dtype('float32'), 8000)
```

### su.embed_image(audio, image, , output=None, output_format=None, overwrite=False, output_dir=None, description='Cover')

Create an audio file with an embedded cover image.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – The audio source — a file path, encoded bytes, a file-like object,
    a numpy waveform / `(waveform, sample_rate)` pair, or a
    `pydub.AudioSegment` (anything [`su.casting.to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_audio_segment)
    accepts).
  * **image** – The cover image — a path, raw image bytes, a file-like object, or a
    PIL `Image`.
  * **output** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Explicit output path. If it has no extension, one is added for the
    resolved format. If None, the path is derived (see module docstring).
  * **output_format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Force the output format (e.g. `'mp3'`, `'flac'`,
    `'m4a'`, `'aiff'`, `'ogg'`, `'opus'`). Overrides the
    input-format-follows rule.
  * **overwrite** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, replace the original file in place (only when the
    output format matches the input’s). Defaults to False — the original
    is never touched.
  * **output_dir** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Directory for derived output paths. Defaults to the input
    file’s directory, or the system Downloads folder for object inputs.
  * **description** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The cover-art description/title stored in the tag.
* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)
* **Returns:**
  The [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) of the written audio file.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If the resolved format cannot embed images, or if
      `overwrite` conflicts with the resolved output.

### Example

```pycon
>>> # File in, cover embedded, format preserved (mp3 stays mp3):
>>> embed_image("song.mp3", "cover.jpg")
PosixPath('song_with_image.mp3')
>>> # Object in (no format) -> flac in Downloads:
>>> import numpy as np
>>> embed_image(np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.int16), "cover.png")
PosixPath('/Users/you/Downloads/audio_with_image.flac')
>>> # Replace the original in place:
>>> embed_image("song.flac", img, overwrite=True)
PosixPath('song.flac')
```

### su.export_audio(src, output=None, , format=None, sample_rate=None, bitrate=None, tags=None, \*\*export_kwargs)

Egress: encode `src` to a chosen format, returning bytes or a path.

This is the controllable-output half of the casting layer. Where the output
format matters, pass `format` (or an `output` path with an extension);
where it does not, omit `output` to get raw bytes you can pipe.

* **Parameters:**
  * **src** – Any supported audio source.
  * **output** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Destination path. If None, encoded bytes are returned instead.
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Target format (`'wav'`, `'mp3'`, `'flac'`, …). Defaults to
    the `output` path’s extension, else `'wav'`.
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional resample target for raw-sample inputs.
  * **bitrate** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional encoder bitrate (e.g. `'192k'` for mp3).
  * **tags** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional metadata tags passed to pydub’s exporter.
  * **\*\*export_kwargs** – Forwarded to `AudioSegment.export()`.
* **Returns:**
  `bytes` if `output` is None, else the [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) written.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> data = export_audio(np.zeros(800, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)
>>> data[:4]  # WAV by default
b'RIFF'
```

### su.recognize(timeout=5, , engine='google')

Quick speech recognition from the microphone (needs the `speech` extra).

* **Parameters:**
  * **timeout** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Maximum seconds to wait for speech.
  * **engine** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Recognition engine (‘google’, ‘sphinx’, ‘wit’, ‘azure’, ‘houndify’).
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### Example

```pycon
>>> text = recognize()
```

### su.speak(text_src, , rate=200, volume=0.9, egress=None, send_to_speakers=True, output_format=None)

Quick text-to-speech with flexible input and output options.

* **Parameters:**
  * **text_src** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO) | [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Any source accepted by [`su.casting.to_text()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_text) (direct text,
    a text-file path/Path, a file-like object, or an iterable of chunks).
  * **rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Speech rate (words per minute).
  * **volume** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Volume level (0.0 to 1.0).
  * **egress** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – 

    Optional output handler:
    - None: no file/bytes output (just speakers, if enabled).
    - str/Path: file path to save audio; the extension (or
      `output_format`) selects the encoding.
    - Callable: receives the synthesized WAV bytes and its return value
      is returned.
  * **send_to_speakers** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to also play the audio through the speakers.
  * **output_format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Explicit output format for a path `egress` (overrides the
    extension). Where format does not matter, use a callable `egress` to
    pipe the raw bytes.
* **Returns:**
  The egress callable’s result, the written [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path), or None.

### Example

```pycon
>>> speak("Hello, world!")
>>> speak("Save this", egress="out.mp3", send_to_speakers=False)
>>> audio = speak("Test", egress=lambda b: b, send_to_speakers=False)
```

### su.to_audio_segment(src, , sample_rate=None, sample_width=None, channels=None)

Cast any supported audio representation to a `pydub.AudioSegment`.

This is the universal ingress (Postel’s “be liberal in what you accept”).

* **Parameters:**
  * **src** – The audio source. See `_SUPPORTED_INPUTS`.
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Sample rate to *assume* for raw-sample inputs (numpy arrays
    / lists). Ignored for encoded inputs, which carry their own rate.
  * **sample_width** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Bytes per sample for raw-sample inputs (inferred if None).
  * **channels** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Channel count for raw-sample inputs (inferred/defaulted to 1).
* **Return type:**
  `AudioSegment`
* **Returns:**
  The audio as an `AudioSegment`.
* **Raises:**
  [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – If `src` is not a supported audio representation.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> seg = to_audio_segment(np.zeros(1000, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=16000)
>>> seg.frame_rate
16000
>>> to_audio_segment(seg) is seg  # AudioSegment passes through unchanged
True
```

### su.to_text(text_src)

Resolve a flexible text source to a plain `str`.

* **Parameters:**
  **text_src** – 

  One of:
  - `str`: direct text, or a file path if it looks like an absolute
    path (starts with the OS path separator or a Windows drive prefix).
  - [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path): path to a UTF-8 text file.
  - file-like: an object with `.read()` (text or binary).
  - iterable of `str`/`bytes` chunks.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Returns:**
  The resolved text.
* **Raises:**
  * [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If a referenced file cannot be read.
  * [**TypeError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#TypeError) – If `text_src` is an unsupported type.

### Example

```pycon
>>> to_text("hello world")
'hello world'
>>> from io import StringIO
>>> to_text(StringIO("streamed text"))
'streamed text'
>>> to_text(iter(["a", "b", "c"]))
'abc'
```

### su.to_wav_bytes(src, \*\*kwargs)

Cast `src` to WAV-encoded [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes).

Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to [`to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.to_audio_segment).

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> to_wav_bytes(np.zeros(800, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)[:4]
b'RIFF'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### su.to_wav_source(src, \*\*kwargs)

Cast `src` to a rewound WAV [`io.BytesIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BytesIO) (for speech_recognition).

Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to [`to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.html.md#su.to_audio_segment).

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> buf = to_wav_source(np.zeros(800, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=8000)
>>> buf.read(4)
b'RIFF'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`BytesIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BytesIO)

### su.to_waveform(src, , sample_rate=None, mono=True, dtype='float32')

Cast `src` to a `(samples, sample_rate)` pair for DSP/ML.

* **Parameters:**
  * **src** – Any supported audio source.
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Desired sample rate of the returned waveform. For encoded
    inputs the audio is resampled to it; for raw-sample inputs it is the
    assumed rate. If None, the source’s native rate is kept.
  * **mono** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Down-mix to a single channel (returns a 1-D array). If False, a
    2-D `(num_samples, num_channels)` array is returned.
  * **dtype** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Output dtype. Float dtypes are normalised to `[-1.0, 1.0]`;
    integer dtypes keep the raw PCM values.
* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]
* **Returns:**
  `(samples, sample_rate)`.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> wf, sr = to_waveform(np.ones(1000, dtype=np.int16), sample_rate=16000)
>>> wf.shape, sr, wf.dtype
((1000,), 16000, dtype('float32'))
```

### su.transcribe(audio_src, , engine='google', debug=False)

Quick transcription of audio from any supported source.

Non-WAV inputs are transcoded to WAV via [`su.casting.to_wav_source()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_wav_source)
(needs ffmpeg) before being handed to the strict recognition core.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio_src** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes) | [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO) | [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)] | [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – Any source accepted by [`su.casting.to_audio_segment()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_audio_segment),
    or a `{'type': 'microphone', 'timeout': N}` dict for live capture.
  * **engine** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Recognition engine (‘google’, ‘sphinx’, ‘wit’, ‘azure’, ‘houndify’).
  * **debug** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Print debug information and re-raise unexpected errors if True.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)
* **Returns:**
  Transcribed text, or None if transcription failed.

### Example

```pycon
>>> text = transcribe("recording.wav")
>>> text = transcribe({'type': 'microphone', 'timeout': 5})
```

# _autosummary/su.words.html.md

# su.words

Word-timestamped transcription of speech, including speech under music.

`transcribe_words(audio)` runs these steps, each a keyword-argument seam with a
working default:

1. **decode** — any container, through [`su.casting.to_waveform()`](_autosummary/su.casting.html.md#su.casting.to_waveform) (ffmpeg via
   pydub; bytes and file-likes never need to touch disk), at its own sample rate.
2. **separate** — keep the voice, drop the instrument: Demucs `htdemucs`’s vocals
   stem ([`demucs_separator()`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.demucs_separator)), at the model’s rate. `separation=False` skips
   it, for speech without music.
3. **detect_speech** — where someone speaks: Silero VAD at threshold 0.3, with tight
   region edges ([`silero_speech_regions()`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.silero_speech_regions)).
4. **recognise** — faster-whisper `large-v3` (int8) with word timestamps, \*\*no
   initial prompt\*\* (Whisper copies a prompt into silent stretches) and
   `condition_on_previous_text=False` ([`whisper_recogniser()`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.whisper_recogniser)).
5. **drop** — segments that are Whisper’s known hallucinations (“Subtitles by
   Amara”, long runs of one character) are set apart ([`is_hallucination()`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.is_hallucination)).
6. **align** — torchaudio’s `MMS_FA` forced alignment, per segment, moves each
   word’s boundaries to its 20 ms frame ([`mms_aligner()`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.mms_aligner)). A spoken capital
   letter is aligned by its name (“B” as “bee”). An alignment that lands far from
   Whisper’s time is not trusted. `alignment=False` keeps Whisper’s times.

The result ([`WordTranscript`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.WordTranscript)) keeps Whisper’s own word times beside the aligned
ones, the speech regions, the speech regions no word covers (“untranscribed
speech”), and the dropped segments, so a caller can judge what to trust.

The default models are made once per process and reused across calls; pass your own
seams to control that.

Needs the `transcribe` extra (demucs, faster-whisper, torch, torchaudio) and
ffmpeg. All heavy imports are lazy, so `import su.words` costs nothing.

Known limit: a single spoken letter under a chord stays unreliable (runs vary between
reruns); use such words as anchors, and label from another signal where it matters.

### Example

```pycon
>>> t = transcribe_words("session.m4a")
>>> [(w.text, round(w.start, 2)) for w in t.words][:3]
[('I', 0.52), ("I'm", 0.6), ('signing', 0.82)]
```

### su.words.ALIGN_PAD_S *= 0.2*

Seconds of audio kept around a segment when aligning it (words at its edges).

### su.words.DFLT_VAD_THRESHOLD *= 0.3*

VAD threshold that keeps quiet speech under an instrument (Silero’s default is 0.5).

### su.words.KNOWN_HALLUCINATIONS *: [frozenset](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]* *= frozenset({'please subscribe', 'subtitles by amara', 'subtitles by the amaraorg community', 'thank you', 'thank you for watching', 'thanks for watching', 'ご視聴ありがとうございました'})*

Phrases Whisper produces from silence or music (subtitle credits and the like). A
segment is dropped only when its whole text, without punctuation, is one of these.

### su.words.LETTER_NAMES *= {'b': 'bee', 'c': 'see', 'd': 'dee', 'e': 'ee', 'f': 'eff', 'g': 'gee', 'h': 'aitch', 'i': 'eye', 'j': 'jay', 'k': 'kay', 'l': 'ell', 'm': 'em', 'n': 'en', 'o': 'oh', 'p': 'pee', 'q': 'cue', 'r': 'ar', 's': 'ess', 't': 'tee', 'u': 'you', 'v': 'vee', 'w': 'doubleyou', 'x': 'ex', 'y': 'why', 'z': 'zee'}*

How a spoken capital letter sounds, for aligning it by pronunciation. “A” is left
out: at a sentence start it is far more often the article.

### su.words.MAX_ALIGN_SHIFT_S *= 1.0*

An aligned word further than this (seconds) from Whisper’s time keeps Whisper’s.

### su.words.MIN_CHAR_RUN *= 8*

A run of one repeated character (letters only) at least this long is a hallucination.

### su.words.MIN_TOKEN_RUN *= 8*

A run of one repeated token at least this long is a hallucination.

### su.words.MIN_UNTRANSCRIBED_S *= 0.3*

A speech region at least this long with no word in it is reported as untranscribed.

### su.words.MMS_FRAME_SAMPLES *= 320*

MMS_FA’s frame stride, in samples at 16 kHz (20 ms).

### su.words.REGION_MIN_SILENCE_MS *= 200*

Silence that splits the reported speech regions. Tighter than the VAD that gates
Whisper (which merges across 2 s), so a pause between words is not “untranscribed”.

### su.words.REGION_SPEECH_PAD_MS *= 30*

Padding around each reported speech region (Silero’s default, 400 ms, bridges pauses).

### su.words.SAMPLE_RATE *= 16000*

Whisper, the VAD and MMS_FA all work at 16 kHz.

### su.words.demucs_separator(, model='htdemucs', stem='vocals', device=None)

A separator keeping one Demucs stem (default: `htdemucs`’s vocals).

It takes audio at any rate, separates at the model’s rate (44.1 kHz for
htdemucs) and returns the stem at 16 kHz. Runs on MPS or CUDA when available.
The model is loaded on first use.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]

### su.words.is_hallucination(text)

Whether a segment’s text is one of Whisper’s known hallucinations.

That is: nothing but punctuation, exactly a known credit phrase, or a long run of
one repeated character or token. Real speech that merely contains a phrase, or a
short repetition (“no no no”, “la la la la”), is kept.

```pycon
>>> is_hallucination("Subtitles by Amara.")
True
>>> is_hallucination("ささささささささささ")
True
>>> is_hallucination("Please subscribe to my channel, and today we cook rice.")
False
>>> is_hallucination("no no no no")
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### su.words.mms_aligner(, device=None, pad=0.2, max_shift=1.0)

An aligner using torchaudio’s `MMS_FA` (multilingual, romanised a–z).

Each segment is aligned on its own audio, padded by `pad` seconds. A word with
no alignable letters keeps Whisper’s times, and so does one whose aligned start
lands more than `max_shift` seconds from Whisper’s (a forced alignment always
finds *some* place). A segment whose alignment fails keeps Whisper’s times and
is logged. The model is loaded on first use.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.Segment)]], [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.Segment)]]

### su.words.resample(wave, sr, target)

`wave` at `target` Hz (torchaudio’s band-limited resampler; float, no clipping).

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### su.words.silero_speech_regions(, threshold=0.3, min_silence_ms=200, speech_pad_ms=30)

Speech regions, in seconds, from Silero VAD (as bundled with faster-whisper).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]]

### su.words.spoken_form(word)

The letters MMS_FA aligns for a word.

Accents are folded, then lower-case a–z and apostrophes are kept; a capital
letter on its own (other than “A”) becomes its name.

```pycon
>>> spoken_form("B"), spoken_form("I'm,"), spoken_form("café"), spoken_form("a")
('bee', "i'm", 'cafe', 'a')
>>> spoken_form("42")
''
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

  * **recognise** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.Segment)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – segments with timed words (default [`whisper_recogniser()`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.whisper_recogniser)).
  * **drop** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]) – `text -> bool`, which segments to set apart as hallucinations.
  * **align** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.Segment)]], [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.Segment)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – refine word times (default [`mms_aligner()`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.mms_aligner)).
  * **separation** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – `False` skips separation, for speech without music.
  * **alignment** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – `False` keeps Whisper’s word times.
* **Return type:**
  [`WordTranscript`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.WordTranscript)

### su.words.uncovered(regions, words, , min_len)

The parts of `regions` no word covers, at least `min_len` long.

```pycon
>>> w = Word("hi", 1.0, 1.5, 1.0, 1.5)
>>> uncovered([(0.0, 3.0)], [w], min_len=0.3)
((0.0, 1.0), (1.5, 3.0))
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]

### su.words.whisper_recogniser(, model='large-v3', compute_type='int8', vad_threshold=0.3, language=None, device='auto')

A faster-whisper recogniser with word timestamps, gated by Silero VAD.

Tuned for speech under music: no initial prompt, no conditioning on previous
text. The model is loaded on first use.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Segment`](_autosummary/su.words.html.md#su.words.Segment)]]
